rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "Big Idea" narratively defines "the first compound loop" in its own sentences (orient / fix tests-first / retro into CLAUDE.local.md / "the fourth move" = ticket close) — a coined term earning itself in the same chunk it's introduced, not an unresolved referent. chunk 5 "Key Concepts" reuses "The loop is orient -> fix -> compound -> close", consistent with chunk 1. chunk 6 "Homework": "The loop's fourth move" echoes chunk 1's own "The fourth move" phrase verbatim. chunk 7 "Next": "plan mode" resolves against chunk 1 ("fix tests-first without plan mode") and chunk 3 ("no plan mode"), both earlier in the same file. No pronoun/demonstrative found anywhere in the body whose antecedent fails to resolve under the sequential read.

chunk 2 "Prework": "the prework at the top of this workbook" is a navigational pointer to a real document location, exempt per carve-out. chunk 8 names its two pre-reads by title/author ("Boris Cherny, Mastering Claude Code in 30 minutes"; "Multi-session and Git: survival guide") rather than by position. No "the opening lecture said..." style positional callback to another file found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal live-demo beat appears anywhere in the body — nothing for this rule to bind to.

Every chunk (1 Big Idea, 2 Prework, 3 What You'll Learn, 4 Start here, 5 Key Concepts, 6 Homework, 7 Next, 8 Pre-reads) carries a self-carrying paragraph or bulleted claim, not a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Each header's content matches its label under the sequential read (e.g. "Homework" = the take-home ticket-close exercise; "Pre-reads before Module 2" = exactly two optional pre-reads before M2); none of the chunk content contradicts its own header.
No "Not X. Not Y. Z." constructions, anaphora/epistrophe triples, self-grading superlatives, number+own-retraction, abstraction-noun stacks, or empty-leg verb triplets found in any of the 9 chunks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 8 "Pre-reads before Module 2": line 57: "**Watch: Boris Cherny, [Mastering Claude Code in 30 minutes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6eBSHbLKuN0).**" bolds a full ~9-word lead sentence, not a short handle; line 59: "**Read: [Multi-session and Git: survival guide](../../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/multi-session-git.md).**" does the same (~6 words, a complete sentence) — two bolded full-sentence leads on one slide, over both the 5-word handle cap and the <=1-bolded-element budget. (Note: chunk 3's four LO bullets each bold a single Bloom's verb — Run / Introspect / Fix / Compound — which is the architecture-mandated checklist-item-name pattern and the compendium's own "one handle per law" allowance; not flagged.)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim each bold span down to the imperative label alone ("Watch:" / "Read:"); let the title and description that follow run as unbolded prose.
